P. 26(b)(5)(A)' in paragraph 4 regarding privilege waiver. The criterion is clearly satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Challenges boilerplate overbreadth objections
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly challenges Corbin's boilerplate objections throughout. Section III (Legal Standard) cites Josephs v. Harris Corp. for the proposition that mere statements of 'overly broad, burdensome, oppressive and irrelevant' are inadequate. Section IV.C is titled 'Corbin's Boilerplate General Objections Should Be Stricken' and directly argues that incorporating general objections into every response violates Rules 33(b)(4) and 34(b)(2)(B)-(C) and the CMO. Section IV.D argues that overbreadth/burden objections require specific factual support (declarations, cost estimates) that Corbin never provided. The Appendix A chart repeatedly labels specific objections as 'boilerplate' and notes they lack factual support. The motion clearly and repeatedly challenges overbreadth objections as boilerplate and legally insufficient.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: States objecting party bears burden of justification
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly states the burden-shifting principle in Section III (Legal Standard): 'A party moving to compel bears the initial burden of showing relevance; the burden then shifts to the objecting party to show specifically why discovery should not be had.' It also cites Josephs v. Harris Corp. for the proposition that a mere boilerplate objection is insufficient, and Section IV.D reiterates that 'An objecting party claiming undue burden must show specifically how each interrogatory is not relevant or how each question is overly broad, burdensome or oppressive.' This clearly states that Corbin, as the objecting party, bears the burden of justifying its objections with specificity.

The motion thus specifically and directly challenges the trade secret objection to RFP No. 5.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Argues trade secret claim requires protective order motion
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly argues in Section IV.E that the remedy for legitimate confidentiality concerns is a protective order under Rule 26(c), requiring 'good cause' through particularized demonstration of harm. It further cites CMO § 4.7 which 'expressly requires that any trade-secret claim be presented by a motion for protective order identifying the specific information claimed as a trade secret and the factual and legal basis for such claim,' and notes that Corbin has done none of this. The motion also argues that Corbin 'cannot object that no protective order exists while refusing to negotiate one.' This clearly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes Corbin failed to identify specific trade secrets

The motion further states that 'Broad allegations of harm, unsubstantiated by specific examples or articulated reasoning, do not satisfy the Rule 26(c) test' (citing Cipollone). The motion also argues that much of what Corbin labels proprietary is actually Vantage's own specification data, not Corbin's trade secrets. This clearly raises the lack of specificity in Corbin's trade secret claims.

For example: 'Corbin cannot locate 35 of the 47 CoCs (74.5%)' in the motion itself, and in the memorandum: 'Corbin produced CoCs for only 12 of 47 purchase orders and asserts that the remaining 35 "cannot be located after a diligent search."' The RFP 22 entry in Appendix A also states: 'produced 12 CoCs (CORBIN-000127--246); remaining 35 "cannot be located after a diligent search."' Both numbers (12 and 47) are correctly and consistently stated throughout the document.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Allegheny Materials Testing by name
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion explicitly identifies Allegheny Materials Testing, Inc. ("AMT") by name as Corbin's metallurgical testing subcontractor in connection with RFP No. 37. In the Appendix A summary chart under RFP 37, the entry reads: 'Corbin--AMT communications re Type 347 testing, VES-4400, tensile/Charpy/IGC testing (2021--present)' and Corbin's objection references 'AMT confidentiality/consent required.' The subcontractor is also named throughout the memorandum of law in Section I (the Foss email discussion), Section IV.I (dedicated to AMT), and in the proposed order paragraph 3.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 22 specifically regarding CoCs
criteria_results.reasoning: RFP No. 22 is explicitly identified by number in multiple places throughout the motion in connection with the CoC production issue. In the motion itself (paragraph 3(e)), it references the missing CoCs. In the memorandum Section H, it discusses the missing CoCs and references 'Req. Nos. 22, 31.' In Appendix A Part 2, RFP 22 is listed with the subject 'CoCs for each shipment Apr. 2021–Dec. 2023, with underlying inspection/test data' and addresses Corbin's deficient response (produced only 12 of 47 CoCs, remaining 35 'cannot be located'). The proposed order paragraph 6 also references the 47 purchase orders and missing Certificates. RFP No. 22 is clearly and specifically identified by number in connection with the CoC production issue.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 31 specifically regarding retention policies
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically identifies RFP No. 31 by number in multiple places. In Section IV.H of the Memorandum, it states 'Corbin's refusal to produce its document retention and destruction policies on relevance grounds (Resp. to Req. No. 31) is untenable.' In the proposed Order, paragraph 6 compels production of retention policies. In Appendix A Part 2, RFP 31 is listed with the description 'Retention/destruction policies and litigation hold notices, 2020–present,' Corbin's objection ('irrelevant; not proportional; overbroad. Refused.'), and Vantage's position challenging that objection. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Addresses RFP No. 37 specifically regarding Allegheny communications
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion specifically identifies RFP No. 37 by number in multiple places. In Appendix A (Part 2), there is a row explicitly labeled 'RFP 37' describing it as 'Corbin–AMT communications re Type 347 testing, VES-4400, tensile/Charpy/IGC testing (2021–present),' noting Corbin's objection based on 'AMT confidentiality/consent required; overbroad; burdensome,' and Vantage's position that 'third-party confidentiality' is not a privilege and that MSA § 14.3.3 forecloses the objection. Additionally, Section I of the Memorandum of Law references RFP Nos. 36–38 and specifically addresses the AMT communications and the third-party confidentiality objection. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Fact discovery deadline correctly stated as March 31, 2025
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum of law states 'With fact discovery closing on March 31, 2025, Vantage respectfully asks the Court to compel complete responses.' This matches the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Correctly attributes evasive Interrogatory 18 response language
criteria_results.reasoning: The motion quotes Corbin's Interrogatory No. 18 response as stating Corbin is 'not aware of any parts that "failed" internal quality inspection and were thereafter shipped to Vantage.' This language appears multiple times in the document (in the motion itself, the memorandum, and the summary chart) and accurately captures the evasive nature of the response. The quote is consistent and correctly attributed throughout the document.
